questions.q: What does it mean that Salesforce was built "API-first"?
options: Almost every action available in the Salesforce UI has a corresponding API call that does the same thing programmatically
The API is only available to Salesforce's own internal engineers, not customers
Salesforce only offers an API for reading data, never for writing it
The Salesforce UI is generated dynamically by calling an AI model
questions.explain: API-first means the platform's capabilities are exposed through APIs as a first-class design choice, so external systems can do almost anything a human admin could do by clicking in the UI.

questions.q: Which API family is purpose-built for loading millions of records asynchronously, rather than one record at a time in real time?
options: Streaming API
Bulk API 2.0
Metadata API
SOAP API
questions.explain: Bulk API 2.0 is designed specifically for high-volume asynchronous data loads, in contrast to REST or SOAP, which are better suited to single or few-record real-time operations.

questions.q: What is the Metadata API actually used for, as distinct from the REST or Bulk APIs?
options: Deploying and retrieving an org's configuration (fields, objects, flows, profiles), not its application data
Running real-time SOQL queries against records
Sending push notifications when a record changes
Loading large volumes of customer records
questions.explain: The Metadata API moves configuration/metadata (what the org looks like), not the records stored inside it — that distinction separates it from every data-moving API in this course.

questions.q: What three things do all of Salesforce's APIs share, according to this lesson?
options: A base URL tied to the org, a version number in the request, and required authentication
They are all XML-based and use the same WSDL contract
They are all free of any rate limits
They can all be called without any authentication, as long as the org allows it
questions.explain: Every Salesforce API call targets an org-specific base URL, specifies an API version, and requires authentication — these three things are constant across REST, SOAP, Bulk, Metadata, and Streaming.

questions.q: A warehouse system needs to be told within seconds whenever an Order's status changes, without constantly polling Salesforce to check. Which API family is this lesson pointing toward?
options: Bulk API 2.0
Metadata API
Streaming API (or its modern successors, Platform Events / Change Data Capture)
SOAP API
questions.explain: Streaming API and its newer forms (Platform Events, Change Data Capture) push real-time notifications of changes, which is exactly what avoids the need to repeatedly poll for updates.
